boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Pleasant Hill record (April 9, 1864) in the Red River Campaign [March-April 1864]. Mansfield on April 8 and the retreat to Grand Ecore on April 10-11 are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, river operations and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Red River Expeditionary Force (Banks's Department of the Gulf) [US] and District of West Louisiana [CS]; the live field reads zero, and NPS says Taylor was outnumbered. Taylor's report says that with 12,000 men he attacked twenty-odd thousand. Irwin says the Union army can hardly have numbered more than 13,000 nor less than 11,000; that Kirby Smith's figures account for 16,000 Confederates while Taylor owns to 12,000; and that the numbers seem to have been nearly equal.
claims.rationale: Interested and retrospective estimates without an inspected return; Irwin's range includes cavalry he says was not engaged. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory and the live result Union Victory. Taylor's order calls it the soldier's victory, and his report says the expedition was defeated and that he held Pleasant Hill next morning after the enemy retreated in the night. Irwin quotes Kirby Smith that Taylor's troops were finally repulsed and thrown into confusion, notes that the earliest Confederate dispatches claimed a signal victory, and says the Confederates were pushed back about a mile with a loss of five guns. NPS says Banks won but retreated.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Banks's retreat and the abandonment of the Shreveport objective are campaign context.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 3,100 total (US 1,100; CS 2,000); the live field reads 2995 (US 1369; CS 1626). Irwin gives the Union loss as 152 killed, 859 wounded and 495 missing, 1,506 in all, with Emory's division 725, and says Taylor estimated the Confederate loss at 1,500. Taylor says some 400 Union wounded were left in his hands and that the cavalry would swell the loss of both battles to 2,500. Irwin's appendix says the losses of April 8 and 9 could not be separated.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The two-day totals belong to both LA018 and LA019 and are not split or added.

open_questions: Banks's, A. J. Smith's, Mower's, Emory's and the brigade and regimental reports, Kirby Smith's report (No. 93, quoted by Irwin), Cunningham's narrative (No. 94), Parsons's and Tappan's reports (Nos. 97-98), Bee's report (No. 99) and the returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Richard B. Irwin's History of the Nineteenth Army Corps (Putnam's, 1892) is a retrospective history by the former assistant adjutant-general of the corps and of Banks's Department of the Gulf, an interested Union account; it cites the Official Records and gives Taylor's and Kirby Smith's figures, so it is not independent of them. Taylor's April 18, 1864 report, his March 13-14 letters printed as its inclosures, his April 24-May 19 dispatches and his April 11 general order are one family of interested Confederate accounts. Official Records Series I, Volume XXXIV, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
